title: Parking Brake Shoe Adjustment — SVT Performance Package
introduction:
On the 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package, the parking brake shoes work inside the drum portion of the rear brake disc. That means the disc has another job hiding inside its hat.

I use the drum’s measured inside diameter to set the shoes’ outside diameter—a measured fit, like sizing a lid to its container. This procedure covers that adjustment and uses the linked brake-disc, wheel-removal and lifting instructions for access and reassembly. Completion includes the specified brake-pedal check; this is not a parking-brake holding-performance test.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Begin on hard, level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling. Otherwise the vehicle could start unexpectedly and cause serious injury or death. If the menu needs power, keep the valid key inside; from confirmed OFF press and release START/STOP without either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON with the engine stopped, retain ON. After the setting change, return ON to OFF without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave OFF. From the ground-accessible cabin, select Neutral on the manual transmission while the parking brake and chocks prevent movement. With ignition OFF, remove the key before service. Keep the parking brake applied until the car is securely raised as described below.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Ignoring these precautions can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Control brake dust and chemical exposure
items.detail: Do not breathe friction-material dust or blow it from components or storage containers with compressed air. Remove it using government-approved techniques. This dust can present cancer and lung-disease hazards, irritate skin, eyes and airways, and cause allergic reactions or other chronic effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified cleaner or lubricant; improper use can cause serious injury. Keep solvents away from ignition sources because they can ignite or explode.

items.name: Review the applicable safety references
items.detail: Before starting, review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189), [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183) and [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Use the prescribed hoist setup
items.detail: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Confirm that its capacity covers the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the stamped triangles marking the lifting points along the underside of the body near the front and rear wheels, and position the arms using [Jacking and Lifting — Overview](#/document/G1663631), section 100-02. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious injury. Incorrect hoist-arm positioning can cause unintended movement, serious injury or death. Do not power the drive wheels with the engine unless all drive wheels are off the ground.

items.name: Keep lifting equipment clear of vulnerable parts
items.detail: Position adapters and hoist forks clear of suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped; also protect the axle and rear cover. Contact can damage these parts. Check underbody clearance before driving onto a drive-on lift. Never lift against either bumper because the covers will be damaged. The vehicle’s emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire, not this service. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; it can lower unexpectedly and cause serious injury. Use floor stands whenever jack support is involved.

items.name: Handle the wheel safely
items.detail: If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; failure to do so can cause serious injury. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut because it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Use the removal and installation instructions in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

items.name: Release and restore the parking brake in a supported state
items.detail: After raising the car and engaging the hoist supporting locks, confirm all wheels are fully clear of the ground. Have a floor-standing helper safely reach the parking-brake lever and release it before cable disconnection and shoe adjustment. If needed, lower the hoist to a securely supported, safely reachable height while keeping every wheel clear; do not climb into the raised car. Keep all ground wheels chocked throughout transitions. Only after complete brake, cable and wheel reassembly and the pedal check, clear everyone from underneath and have the floor-standing helper reapply the parking brake before lowering. Keep the lowering path clear of people and tools; restore wheel chocks as the tires reach ground before hoist support ends. Once fully grounded and chocked, hold the clutch pedal down and select first gear from the ground-accessible cabin, retaining the parking brake and ignition OFF/key out for final wheel-nut torque.

items.name: Have the adjustment and access equipment ready
items.detail: Have a caliper gauge suitable for the drum inside diameter and the widest shoe outside diameter, a way to record measurements, and a flat-bladed screwdriver for the adjuster opening. Have a caliper support hook, wire brush, torque equipment and new caliper mounting bolts ready. Discard the removed mounting bolts.

items.name: Use the specified cleaning and lubrication materials
items.detail: Have Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, for the disc mating surfaces, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only for the wheel pilot-bore/hub-pilot interface. Complete the dust-control steps below before mating-face cleaning; the wire brush is for corrosion on the mating faces, not dispersing friction dust.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage.

edits.text: Remove the brake disc using [Brake Disc - Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package](#/document/G1716401) (206-04 Rear Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why:
Removing the disc exposes both the drum’s inner surface and the parking brake shoes. After completing the lifting preparation, remove the wheel nuts and lift the wheel-and-tire assembly off the hub. Unhook the parking brake cable end from the shoe actuation lever beside the coil spring. At the cable-housing bracket, press the fitting’s retaining tabs inward and withdraw the fitting from the bracket.

Arrange the caliper support hook before releasing its mounting. Remove and discard the caliper mounting bolts, remove the bracket, then position the caliper aside with a support hook. Do not let the caliper hang from its brake hose: that can damage the hose. Remove the disc from the hub. These access details come from the linked procedure, whose removal instructions also contain information needed during installation.

edits.text: Use the Caliper Gauge to measure the inside diameter (ID) of the drum portion of the brake disc. Record the measurement.
edits.why: Measure across the opposed inner drum surfaces indicated by the arrows, not across the central hub opening or the disc’s outer edge. I keep this recorded measurement beside the gauge because it is the reference for setting the shoes.

edits.text: Use the Caliper Gauge to measure the widest outside diameter across the parking brake shoes.
edits.why: Place the gauge across the opposing outer lining surfaces shown by the arrows. The widest span is the dimension that must fit inside the drum; measuring a narrower part of the assembly would give a misleading comparison.

edits.text: Remove the small oval access plug from the rear face of the backing plate.
edits.why: The plug is shown in blue alongside the suspension and driveshaft. Removing it opens the screwdriver access to the shoe adjuster.

edits.text: Through the backing-plate opening, use a flat-bladed screwdriver to rotate the shoe adjuster. Remeasure the widest shoe diameter and continue adjusting until it is 0.59 mm (0.023 in) less than the recorded ID of the drum portion of the brake disc.
edits.why: The screwdriver engages the toothed adjuster shown in yellow. Check the measured change as you turn it to establish whether the shoes are moving outward or inward; the drawing does not specify a clockwise or counterclockwise direction. The specified difference compares the complete shoe diameter with the drum’s inside diameter—it is not a gap to apply independently at each shoe. I let the gauge settle the fit rather than judging it by eye.

edits.text: Refit the access plug in the backing-plate opening.
edits.why: This closes the adjuster access after the measured shoe diameter has been set.

edits.text: Install the brake disc using [Brake Disc - Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package](#/document/G1716401) (206-04 Rear Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why:
For reassembly, clean the brake-disc mating surfaces with a wire brush and the specified brake-parts cleaner before bringing those surfaces together. Refit the disc, return the supported caliper to position, reinstall the bracket and use new caliper mounting bolts tightened to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm). Reattach the cable-housing fitting in its bracket and reconnect the cable end to the parking brake shoe actuation lever, reversing the removal sequence.

Before refitting the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its mounting surface and the mating hub/disc surface. Make sure any rotor-to-hub fasteners are secured clear of those mating surfaces. Failure to do this can let the wheel nuts loosen and the wheel come off while driving, causing loss of control, serious injury or death. Apply only a thin coat of the specified anti-seize at the wheel pilot-bore/hub-pilot interface. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc/drum mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces to avoid component damage.

Position the wheel and install its nuts finger tight initially. Before lowering, with full brake, cable and wheel reassembly complete, remove all tools and keep hands and everyone clear of the assembled brake mechanisms before any pedal operation. Have the floor-standing helper safely reach the brake pedal without climbing into the raised car; if needed use the securely supported reachable height described in preparation. Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct operation. If operation is abnormal, keep the vehicle out of use for matching diagnosis. Clear everyone from underneath, have the helper reapply the parking brake, then lower and restore wheel restraints as described in preparation. Once fully grounded and chocked, hold the clutch pedal down and select first gear with ignition OFF. With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the nuts in the star/cross pattern shown in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads. Skipping that pattern can produce excessive disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration. Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi): wheels can loosen after initial tightening, with a risk of serious injury.

editorialRevision.scope: Manual-only known-state setup/secure-height parking release and restoration, exact specified material names, EPA dust controls before mating-face preparation, supported caliper handover and ordinary pedal-check coordination. Primary action text, all dimensions and torques unchanged.
